Assemble a DNA methylation cohort from one or more arrays

Source: R/methylationCohort.R
methylationCohort.Rd

Gathers beta values from any mix of Infinium arrays (HM450, EPIC, EPICv2, ...) with their sample information and genomic positions, for methylationTrack() and its module. Arrays are joined on genomic position rather than on probe ID: the same cg ID can sit at different positions on different arrays, and different IDs can measure the same CpG, so a join on IDs would merge what should not be merged and split what should. Nothing is joined up front. A region is pulled from each array when it is asked for, so an HDF5-backed SummarizedExperiment::SummarizedExperiment() stays out of memory, and a cohort's full union of CpGs, over a million rows, is never built.

Usage

methylationCohort(
  betas,
  samples = NULL,
  probes = NULL,
  genome = "hg38",
  assay = NULL,
  txns = NULL,
  cytobands = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'methylationCohort'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

betas

The beta values, in one of the forms described in Details.

samples

Optional data frame of sample information.

probes

Optional probe positions: a GRanges named by probe ID, or a list of them named as betas is.

genome

The genome build, such as "hg38".

assay

For a SummarizedExperiment, the assay holding beta values. By default one named betas, beta or Beta, else the first.

txns

Optional transcripts as a GRangesList of exons, one element per transcript named by transcript ID, with gene_name in its mcols(). Its transcript_type, cdsStart and cdsEnd are used where present. The shape of genomeInfo$txns from sesameData::sesameData_getGenomeInfo().

cytobands

Optional data frame of cytobands, with chrom, chromStart, chromEnd and gieStain columns.

x

A methylationCohort.

...

Ignored.

Value

A methylationCohort object: a list holding arrays (each with its betas, loci and rowdata), samples, genome, txns, cytobands and dropped (the rows left out).

x, invisibly.

Details

Input forms. betas is one of:

  • A named list with one matrix or SummarizedExperiment per array, named by platform (list(HM450 = m1, EPIC = m2, EPICv2 = m3)). A CpG is on an array when that array has a row for it.

  • One matrix or SummarizedExperiment already merged across arrays, with NA where a sample's array lacks a probe. Sample information can name each sample's array in a platform column; a CpG is then on an array when any of that array's samples has a value there. Without one, the cohort cannot tell a probe the array lacks from one that failed, and both are drawn in the NA colour.

Matrices have probe IDs as row names and samples as columns.

Positions. Each array's positions come from the first of these it has:

  1. probes, a GRanges named by probe ID, or a list of them named by platform.

  2. The rowRanges() of a SummarizedExperiment. These must be on genome.

  3. rowData() columns: CpG_chrm and CpG_beg, as in the Infinium annotation manifests, whose BED-style starts are shifted to one-based; or chr and pos, as in minfi's annotation packages, taken as they are. Check that they are on genome: minfi's HM450 and EPIC annotations are often hg19.

  4. The sesameData manifest of the array, found from its platform name (HM450 or 450K, EPIC, EPICv2, MSA or HM27). These hold hg38 only, so another genome needs one of the above.

Probe IDs match exactly, then on the ID's prefix, so cg00000029_TC21 finds cg00000029 and the reverse. In a merged matrix, an ID is looked up on each array in turn, newest first.

Rows that cannot be placed, and SNP (rs), control (ctl) and nucleotide variant (nv) probes, are left out, and counted when the cohort is printed. So is the number of CpGs each pair of arrays shares: a pair sharing few suggests its positions disagree, such as one on another genome build.

Samples. Sample information comes from each SummarizedExperiment's colData() and from samples, whose row names or one of whose columns must hold the column names of betas. Both are kept, samples taking precedence. The table gains sample and, for a list of arrays, platform columns. A sample run on two arrays stays as two samples, with the platform added to each name.

Annotation. With txns and cytobands left as NULL, the transcripts and cytobands of genome are read from sesameData when they are first needed, and held for the session. Where neither is available those tracks are not drawn and genes cannot be looked up.

Beta values are not adjusted between arrays. Differences between platforms remain, so check for them by grouping samples on platform.

See also

methylationTrack(), methylationTrackApp()

Author

Jared Andrews

Examples

betas <- matrix(
    c(0.1, 0.9, 0.5, 0.2, 0.8, 0.4),
    nrow = 3, dimnames = list(c("cg1", "cg2", "cg3"), c("a", "b"))
)
probes <- GenomicRanges::GRanges("chr1", IRanges::IRanges(c(100, 200, 300), width = 2))
names(probes) <- rownames(betas)
cohort <- methylationCohort(
    list(HM450 = betas), probes = probes,
    samples = data.frame(tissue = c("Blood", "Liver"), row.names = c("a", "b"))
)
cohort
#> methylationCohort: 2 samples on hg38 
#>   HM450          2 samples          3 probes
